**Align Avalanche Network Growth with AVAX Holder Value**

**Avalanche has outstanding technology, fast finality, and a rapidly growing ecosystem in RWA, stablecoins, and institutional adoption. However, the market’s biggest concern today is not whether Avalanche is successful—it is whether the value created by the network ultimately accrues to AVAX holders.**

**Today, there is a visible disconnect between network growth and token performance. Institutional adoption continues to increase, yet AVAX has not fully captured the value generated by the ecosystem.**

**I believe Avalanche should gradually strengthen its value capture model by considering initiatives such as:**

**Requiring enterprise L1s (formerly Subnets) to lock AVAX for long-term network participation.**
**Allowing governance to optimize the fee model over time as the ecosystem matures, instead of maintaining permanently minimal fees.**
**Using a portion of protocol revenue generated by RWA, stablecoins, and enterprise applications to support AVAX through buybacks, burns, or staking rewards.**
**Increasing AVAX’s utility within validators, enterprise infrastructure, and institutional deployments so that ecosystem growth naturally drives token demand.**
**Transitioning staking rewards toward real network revenue instead of relying primarily on token emissions.**

**Avalanche does not need to become the most expensive blockchain. Instead, it should become the blockchain where network value and token value are strongly aligned.**

**The long-term goal should be simple:**

**Network Growth → AVAX Demand → AVAX Holder Value**

**If Avalanche achieves this alignment, AVAX will no longer be viewed merely as a gas token, but as the core asset representing the growth of the entire Avalanche economy.**

Hey everyone — quick heads up.

I’m going to follow up with a few people here individually about Ekko / WalletAlert over the next few days.

This is not spam, not a token thing, not an airdrop, and not anything that requires connecting a wallet, signing a transaction, downloading a file, or clicking anything suspicious.

We’re doing this because this group is genuinely one of the best places for us to ask for feedback. You’re active in the Avalanche ecosystem, you understand the needs of Web3 products, and many of you are building, advising, investing in, or working with protocols directly.

We’ve had the Ekko API in public beta for the past few months, and it’s now ready for broader use. As part of that, we’re releasing **WalletAlert**, the first direct user-facing interface built on top of Ekko.

A simple way to think about WalletAlert:

**WalletAlert is an onchain inbox for dApps.**

It gives every dApp a wallet-aware notifications centre — a place where protocols can notify, guide, and re-engage users based on wallet activity and protocol events.

WalletAlert can be added to a dApp through a lightweight embed / open-source npm package. The install is designed to be as simple as adding a single line of code.

The idea is simple:

Protocols should not have to rely only on Discord, Telegram, X, or email to reach their users.

With WalletAlert, a dApp can notify users directly inside the product when something relevant happens onchain or inside the protocol.

A key feature of Ekko is natural-language alert creation. Protocols can create alert templates by describing what they want in plain English, and users can create their own wallet-level alerts the same way.

For example:

• “Alert users when rewards are ready to claim”
• “Notify me if my position is close to liquidation”
• “Tell users when they have a governance vote pending”
• “Alert me when my wallet receives more than $1,000”

WalletAlert can help with things like:

• Rewards to claim
• Governance proposals that need attention
• Positions close to liquidation
• Completed staking, vault, or protocol actions
• Unusual wallet activity
• Token unlocks or protocol events
• Missed user actions
• Personalised opportunities or next steps

Over time, the inbox will become more than a feed of alerts. The goal is for it to become an agentic action layer inside the dApp — one that can explain an alert, guide onboarding, recommend the next step, and help users complete actions without leaving the product.

For builders, the goal is to reduce silent churn, improve retention, and create a better communication channel with users.

For users and clients, the goal is to make Web3 products feel more responsive, useful, and safer — because the app can tell them what matters at the right moment instead of hoping they see an announcement somewhere else.

We’re especially keen to work with teams in the **Avalanche ecosystem**, because we’re making WalletAlert free for Avalanche protocols while we collect feedback and shape the product.

We’re not asking anyone to integrate immediately. We’re looking for builders who are willing to give candid feedback on the product, the use cases, and whether this would be useful for their own protocol or clients.

If you’re open to being a feedback partner, you can reply here, DM me, or sign up here:

How we got here
1- Validator roots
We began as pure-play validators, scaling to 150+ servers across 20+ proof-of-stake networks. Every sleepless night chasing five-nines uptime shaped our obsession with reliability.

2- Stepping into Regulated Custody
When a pioneering fund asked for a compliant way to hold its tokens, we secured OAM registration and integrated a Fireblocks-powered custody engine. Suddenly, institutional capital could rest on blockchain rails without sacrificing governance or auditability.

3- Spotting the Yield Gap
Safe storage alone wasn’t enough, assets locked in custody earned nothing. We saw a critical gap between security and yield generation that no one had bridged.

4- Building Institutional Hub
Our answer was the Institutional Hub:
• Delegate, earn, and vote directly from the custody provider you trust.
• Route stakes to the validator you choose, no key exposure, no workflow sprawl.
• Generate compliant on-chain yield while your signatures, policies, and audit trails stay fully in-house.

Why we’re changing now

🔹 A refreshed Colossus Digital brand: new look, sharper language, clearer resources.
🔹 Institutional Hub v3.0: rebuilt for scalability, deeper reporting, and seamless multi-custody orchestration.
